NONE: C1 a person, group, etc. competing with others for the same thing or in the same area
C2 to be as good, clever, beautiful, etc. as someone or something else

example: He beat his closest/nearest rival by 20 marks.
他以領先20分的成績打敗了和他水平最接近的對手。
The companies produce rival versions of the toy.
這些公司生産的玩具跟我們的産品爭奪市場。
No computer can rival a human brain for/in complexity.
沒有任何電腦比得上人腦複雜。
The beauty of the country is only rivalled by (= is as great in degree as) the violence of its politics.
該國的美麗風光非同尋常，而其國內政治的殘暴同樣驚世駭俗。

NONE: C2 a situation in which people, businesses, etc. compete with each other for the same thing

example: There's such rivalry among/between my three sons.
我的三個兒子相互較勁，鬧得不可開交。
There's fierce rivalry for the job/to get the job.
很多人想要得到這份工作，競爭非常激烈。
It was a community/nation/family riven by hatred.
這是個由於仇恨變得四分五裂的社區／國家／家庭。

NONE: A1 a natural wide flow of fresh water across the land into the sea, a lake, or another river
A1 written abbreviation R used before or after the name of a river
（通常用於河流名稱前，有時位於河流名稱後）河
› in the opposite direction to the flow of water in the river
› in the same direction as the flow of water in the river

example: We sailed slowly down the river.
我們順流而下緩緩航行。
the River Thames/Seine/Nile
泰晤士／賽納／尼羅河
the Hudson/Mississippi/Yangzte River
哈德遜河／密西西比河／揚子江
We sailed up river.
我們逆流而行。

NONE: › the land at either edge of a river

example: We sat on the riverbank and had a picnic.
我們坐在河岸上吃了一頓野餐。

NONE: › the ground over which a river usually flows

example: a stony/muddy/dry riverbed
多石的／泥濘的／乾涸的河床

NONE: › a large passenger boat that travels up and down a river
› a large amount of a liquid

example: Rivers of sweat ran down his back.
他汗流浹背。
figurative If there's a revolution, rivers of blood will flow.
如果發生革命，將會血流成河。

NONE: › the land along the edges of a river

example: a riverside restaurant
濱河餐館

NONE: › a metal pin used to fasten flat pieces of metal or other thick materials such as leather
› to fasten parts together with a rivet
› to not be able to stop looking at something because it is so interesting or frightening
（因感到有趣而）目不轉睛地看；（因害怕而）動彈不得，呆若木雞

example: Many parts of an aircraft are riveted together.
飛機很多部件都是鉚接在一起的。
It was an amazing film - I was absolutely riveted.
那部電影太精彩了——我完全被吸引住了。
His eyes were riveted on the television.
他雙眼緊盯著電視看。
He pulled out a gun and I was riveted to the spot (= so frightened that I could not move).
他拔出了槍，我簡直被嚇呆了。
It was a riveting story.
那是個非常動聽的故事。

NONE: › an area of coast, especially one with beaches where people go on holiday

example: the French/Italian/Cornish riviera
法國／義大利／科尼什海濱渡假勝地
figurative Rivulets of sweat/rain/blood ran down his face.
汗水／雨水／鮮血從他臉上不住地流下來。
